# Jubilees Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Three Visitors at Mamre; Sodom Destroyed; Isaac Born; Feast of Tabernacles

---

**16:1** On the first day of the fourth month, we appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre. We spoke with him and told him that Sarah his wife was going to give him a son.

**16:2** Sarah laughed — she had been listening to us talking with Abraham. We confronted her about it.

**16:3** She got frightened and denied it: "I didn't laugh." She was afraid of us.

**16:4** We told her what her son's name would be — the name already recorded and inscribed on the heavenly tablets: Isaac.

**16:5** After we left Abraham, we turned toward Sodom. Abraham walked with us part of the way.

**16:6** The LORD said: "Should I hide from Abraham what I'm about to do? I know he will raise his children and teach his household to follow the LORD's way — to do justice and what is right — so that the LORD can fulfill every promise he made to him."

**16:7** "We are going to destroy this place because of the wickedness of its people before the LORD."

**16:8** Abraham moved close and said: "Are you really going to sweep away the righteous along with the wicked? What if there are fifty righteous people in the city? Wouldn't you spare the whole place for their sake?"

**16:9** "You couldn't possibly do that — kill the righteous with the wicked, treat the righteous the same as the wicked. You couldn't. Isn't the Judge of all the earth supposed to act justly?"

**16:10** The LORD said: "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I'll spare the whole city for their sake."

**16:11** Abraham said: "Look, I've gone out on a limb to speak to the LORD — me, nothing but dust and ashes."

**16:12** He kept pressing — fifty, then forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, ten — and the LORD said: "I won't destroy it for ten."

**16:13** We arrived in Sodom at evening. Lot was sitting at the city gate. When he saw us he jumped up to meet us and bowed his face to the ground.

**16:14** He said: "Please, my lords — come to my house tonight. You can rest, wash your feet, and set out again in the morning."

**16:15** "No," they said, "we'll spend the night in the open square." But Lot pressed them hard, and they came with him to his house.

**16:16** He made them a meal and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.

**16:17** Before they had even lain down to sleep, the men of Sodom surrounded the house — young and old, every man from every part of the city.

**16:18** They shouted to Lot: "Where are the men who came to your house tonight? Send them out. We want to have sex with them."

**16:19** Lot stepped outside, pulled the door shut behind him, and said: "Brothers, please — don't do this terrible thing."

**16:20** "Look, I have two daughters who are still virgins. Let me bring them out to you — do whatever you want with them. But leave these men alone. They're under my roof and under my protection."

**16:21** "Get out of our way," they yelled. "Who do you think you are? You're a foreigner here, and now you're going to lecture us? We'll treat you worse than them." The crowd pressed in hard against Lot and moved to break down the door.

**16:22** The angels reached out, yanked Lot back inside, and slammed the door. Then they struck every man at the door with blindness — young and old alike — and those men groped around helplessly, unable to find the door.

**16:23** The angels said to Lot: "Anyone else here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters — anyone who belongs to you in this city — get them out now."

**16:24** "We're going to destroy this place. The outcry against it has reached the LORD, and he's sent us to level it."

**16:25** Lot went to warn his sons-in-law who were engaged to his daughters: "Leave the city right now — the LORD is going to destroy it." But they thought he was losing his mind.

**16:26** Dawn came, and the angels grabbed Lot: "Up! Take your wife and your two daughters and go — or you'll be caught in the city's punishment."

**16:27** He was still hesitating, so the angels took him by the hand — and his wife, and his two daughters — God being merciful to him — and hauled them physically out of the city.

**16:28** Once they were outside, an angel said: "Run for your life. Don't look back. Don't stop anywhere in this valley. Get to the mountain, or you won't survive."

**16:29** Then the LORD rained fire and burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah from out of heaven.

**16:30** He destroyed those cities, the whole valley, every person in them, and every plant growing in the ground.

**16:31** In this jubilee, the Feast of Tabernacles was established as an everlasting ordinance for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all their descendants.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The sexual violence at Lot's door (v.18) is rendered directly — "have sex with them" conveys the Ge'ez without euphemism. The Sodom episode follows the Genesis narrative closely with Jubilees' angelic perspective inserted. The Feast of Tabernacles (v.31) is a brief but significant Jubilees calendrical projection.*
